name: Eastern Hungarian Kingdom
alt: Kingdom of Hungary under John I and John II

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Hungary
predecessors.text: Transylvania, held by John Zápolya as voivode, and the eastern part of the kingdom he secured at the Treaty of Nagyvárad (1538)

successors.name: Principality of Transylvania
successors.text: Transylvania and the Partium, which the Treaty of Speyer (16 August 1570) left to John Sigismund Zápolya

ledger.x: 10-11 November 1526: John Zápolya is proclaimed and crowned King of Hungary.

July 1527: Ferdinand's German mercenaries enter Hungary against Zápolya, who is beaten at Tarcal near Tokaj on 27 September 1527; Ferdinand is crowned at Székesfehérvár on 3 November 1527 and, by 1528, drives John from the country (he flees to Poland).
24 February 1538: the Treaty of Nagyvárad ends the contest.
1538: John I secures the eastern part of the kingdom at Nagyvárad.

1541: the capital moves from Buda to Lippa after Suleiman takes central Hungary as 'Budin Province' (infobox: Buda 1526-41, Lippa 1541-42, Gyulafehérvár 1542-70); the page says 'In 1541, Ferdinand invaded to enforce his claim' and that Suleiman expelled him and took central Hungary as 'Budin Province'.
1542: the capital moves from Lippa to Gyulafehérvár (Alba Iulia), where it stays to 1570 (infobox).
1547: Cliopatria adds the lands the page lists in the 1540s kingdom (counties such as Békés, Csongrád, Arad, Csanád and the Temesköz; the first pass left Csongrád out of this list).
Summer 1551: the kingdom is dissolved and its land passes to Ferdinand.
16 August 1570: the Treaty of Speyer ends the Eastern Hungarian Kingdom.

wars.name: War between John Zápolya and Ferdinand of Habsburg for the Hungarian crown
wars.outcome: Zápolya beaten at Tarcal (27 September 1527) and exiled to Poland in 1528, restored in 1529 with Ottoman help after becoming a vassal of Suleiman; the 1538 Treaty of Nagyvárad divided the country, the east to John I, the north and west to Ferdinand.

wars.name: Ferdinand's invasion and the Ottoman occupation of central Hungary
wars.outcome: Ferdinand invaded in 1541 to enforce his claim after John I's death; Suleiman expelled him, recognised John II as king and his vassal, and took central Hungary as Budin Province.

wars.name: Struggle for Transylvania between Isabella, Martinuzzi and Ferdinand
wars.outcome: Isabella ceded Transylvania at Nyírbátor (1549); Martinuzzi's army besieged Gyulafehérvár in 1550 and 1551; John II abdicated in 1551; Castaldo's troops left in 1553; the nobles recalled John II in 1556.

certainty.note: The Treaty of Nagyvárad (1538) and the Treaty of Speyer (1570) are not described by lines; the kingdom is Transylvania and counties on the Tisza plain, and the Hungarian-Ottoman frontier moves with each campaign.
